title: Building an Inclusive ProQR
summary: Pride month at ProQR is an opportunity to celebrate and thank all of the LGBT+ people in our communities, including our employees, scientists, and doctors that made our research possible.
body_text: Written by Pride Month June 2022 09 June 2022 At ProQR we strive to create an inclusive culture where everyone is valued for who they are and individual differences and contributions are recognized and appreciated. Therefore, we decided for this Pride Month June 2022, to visually demonstrate our support and acknowledgment of the LGBTQ+ community by changing our logo to incorporate the pride rainbow flag. At ProQR we strive to create an inclusive culture where everyone is valued for who they are and individual differences and contributions are recognized and appreciated. Therefore, we decided for this Pride Month June 2022, to visually demonstrate our support and acknowledgment of the LGBTQ+ community by changing our logo to the pride rainbow flag. What is Pride Month? Pride Month is observed in June all over the world as June marks the anniversary of the Stonewall Riots in the US in 1969. During these riots the LGBT+ community (Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender), particularly those of color, fought back against police harassment and discrimination. This revolution and necessary change could not have been possible without important figures in queer history such as Marsha P. Johnson, Sylvia Rivera, or Stormé DeLarverie and could have not continued without the contribution of the thousands of LGBTQ+ people who are still fighting to achieve and maintain rights and inclusion in society. Pride at ProQR Pride month at ProQR is an opportunity to celebrate and thank all of the LGBT+ people in our communities, including our employees, scientists, and doctors that made our research possible. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive company where everyone feels welcome, heard, and safe to be themselves. We believe it is important to build a safe workplace, not only for those living out and proud, but also for those who are still in their journey of self acceptance. A member of ProQR’s diversity, equity and inclusion team at ProQR Happy #PrideMonth! Tags Inclusivity Share page Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Email

title: Tactile Medical to Release Second Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results on August 10, 2026
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. 's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: MINNEAPOLIS, July 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. (“Tactile Medical”; the “Company”) (Nasdaq: TCMD), a medical technology company providing therapies for people with chronic disorders, today announced that second quarter of fiscal year 2026 financial results will be released after the market closes on Monday, August 10, 2026. Management will host a conference call with a question and answer session at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on August 10, 2026, to discuss the results of the quarter. Those who would like to participate may dial 877-407-3088 (201-389-0927 for international callers) and provide access code 13761142. A live webcast of the call will also be provided on the investor relations section of the Company's website at investors.tactilemedical.com . For those unable to participate, a replay of the call will be available for two weeks at 877-660-6853 (201-612-7415 for international callers); access code 13759535. The webcast will be archived at investors.tactilemedical.com . About Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. (DBA Tactile Medical) Tactile Medical is a leader in developing and marketing at-home therapies for people suffering from underserved, chronic conditions including lymphedema, lipedema, chronic venous insufficiency and chronic inflammatory lung disease by helping them live better and care for themselves. Tactile Medical collaborates with clinicians to expand clinical evidence, raise awareness, increase access to care, reduce overall healthcare costs, and improve the quality of life for tens of thousands of patients each year. Announcing Twilio Lookup Line Status Public Beta: Verify Number Deliverability Before You Send
summary: Optimize SMS campaigns with Twilio's Lookup Line Status, now Public Beta. Maximize deliverability, reduce bounce rates, and safeguard your budget with authoritative data.
body_text: Time to read: July 14, 2026 Written by Catie Kolander Twilion Reviewed by Kelley Robinson Twilion Paul Kamp Twilion Announcing Twilio Lookup Line Status Public Beta: Verify Number Deliverability Before You Send Ever start a One-Time Passcode (OTP) flow or a massive marketing SMS campaign, only to see your bounce rates jump and your budget disappear into the void? Often, businesses didn't validate numbers, they audited failures. They paid for a message, waited for it to bounce, and then tasked engineering with parsing carrier codes like 30003 or 30005 to figure out why. By the time the business got that data, the capital was spent, carrier networks flagged their traffic, and the customer they were trying to authenticate had already walked away. With Twilio Lookup Line Status now officially in Public Beta, it’s time to start putting real-time carrier insights to work. You can now tap directly into mobile operator networks, querying the Home Location Register (HLR) where available, to know instantly if a number is active, inactive, reachable, or unreachable before you ever hit send. Stop wasting resources on dead ends and start using Line Status today to protect your deliverability and optimize your messaging spend. Why Line Status matters for your business By moving phone number validation from a post-delivery audit to a pre-send check, businesses can optimize their communication workflows: Maximize campaign deliverability : Ensure your marketing messages and authentication traffic are directed to valid and reachable recipients. Reduce wasted spend : Stop wasting budget on deactivated lines, invalid numbers, or fake sign-up attempts. Protect your sender reputation : Keep bounce rates low to maintain strong standings with carrier networks across all your outreach campaigns. Streamline database hygiene : Regularly scrub your contact lists or CRMs to eliminate stale, recycled, or deactivated customer data. Supercharge accuracy We know that number intelligence is only as valuable as the data behind it. That's why we have revamped our underlying models for the US market. By integrating advanced real-time data, we have boosted our US accuracy to 99.1% for both active and inactive phone numbers. This unparalleled level of precision minimizes false positives and negatives, giving your team data you can actually trust to fuel automated workflows. How it works Integrating Line Status into your existing registration, onboarding, or messaging pre-flight check is incredibly straightforward. A simple GET request to the Lookup v2 API retrieves the live status of any phone number: Copy code curl -X GET 'https://lookups.twilio.com/v2/PhoneNumbers/+447772000001?Fields=line_status' \ -u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN The API returns a clean, actionable JSON response indicating whether the phone number is currently reachable on the carrier network: Copy code { "calling_country_code": "44", "country_code": "GB", "phone_number": "+447772000001", "national_format": "07772 000001", "valid": true, "validation_errors": null, "caller_name": null, "carrier": null, "sim_swap": null, "call_forwarding": null, "line_status": { "status": "reachable", "error_code": null }, "url": "https://lookups.twilio.com/v2/PhoneNumbers/+447772000001" } The possible statuses are: Active Reachable Unreachable Inactive Unknown Learn more about each status in the documentation. Choosing the right Lookup package Twilio Lookup offers an array of specialized identity packages. Depending on your exact journey stage, you can leverage Line Status alongside our other packages to build a comprehensive fraud and delivery defense: Choose Line Status when your priority is list hygiene, maximizing delivery rates, pruning deactivated numbers, or confirming a device is live right now. Choose Line Type Intelligence (LTI) if you primarily need number routing metadata (distinguishing mobile vs. landline vs. VoIP) or want a low-latency, first-pass filter for channel gating. Choose Reassigned Number if you are texting US consumers and require strict TCPA/regulatory compliance. Line Status checks network reachability, but it does not query the FCC Reassigned Numbers Database (RND). You must use a Reassigned Number with a last-consent date for legal compliance safety. Availability and pricing Lookup Line Status supports phone numbers worldwide. Because the package triggers an authoritative, live query straight to mobile operator networks, you can expect an average lookup response latency of 1.2 seconds, with a P99 latency of 4.1 seconds. Pricing starts at a flat rate per call, with volume-tiered discounting built into the API to automatically lower your costs as your operations scale. Get started today Stop texting and calling into the dark. Clean up your databases, secure your user onboarding, and optimize your delivery spend with authoritative, live carrier signals. Explore the Twilio Lookup Line Status API Documentation to start building with the Public Beta today! Catie is a Principal Product Marketing Manager at Twilio where she works with the User Authentication & Identity Team. Catie has worked with a variety of SaaS and tech companies across telecommunications and identity intelligence industries.

title: Email Security Needs Proof, Not Static Detection: Takeaways from SACR's Email Security Report
summary: Static email defenses are falling short as attackers abuse identity, trust, and business workflows. Learn how the future of email security depends on context, investigation, and proof.
body_text: Varonis security brief Perimeter-based email defenses miss AI-generated attacks that carry no obvious malicious link or attachment. A new report from Software Analyst Cyber Research (SACR) says email security must shift from detecting bad messages to investigating how an attack unfolds. SACR highlights Varonis Interceptor as an example of this shift because it uses an AI Phishing Sandbox that follows an attack through to the credential-harvesting page a user would actually land on. Email security is undergoing a fundamental shift — from static defense to an approach built around identity, context, and evidence — now that attackers have learned to exploit trust, identity, and human judgment to circumvent traditional perimeter-based detection. Software Analyst Cyber Research (SACR) illustrates why in a new report titled From Perimeter to Proof: The New Architecture of Email Security . In it, Anna Perrone, Research Associate/Business Process Analyst at SACR, examines a new generation of email security architectures designed to address the business workflows attackers now regularly exploit through email. Perrone looks at key vendors that represent the new generation of email security, including Varonis Interceptor . The email security solution is highlighted for approaching phishing not as a standalone email problem, but as the first stage of a broader attack chain that can lead to credential theft, data exposure, privilege escalation, or business-process compromise. Perimeter-based email security is not enough Traditional email security was built around static detection and perimeter-based defenses. These solutions identify known threats, flag suspicious messages, and rely on users or downstream controls to respond. But this model is increasingly ineffective against modern attacks . The report identifies context as the core gap in that model. Perimeter-based, content-detection-driven systems are designed to catch known indicators at the point of entry. These solutions have limited ability to evaluate attacks that lack obvious signals like malicious links or attachments. As attackers increasingly use AI to create novel attacks that abuse trusted relationships and communication patterns, context becomes the deciding factor in whether an interaction is legitimate or malicious. Software Analyst Cyber Research (SACR) advocates for a fundamental shift in email security from static defense to protections that examine the entire business workflow. Software Analyst Cyber Research (SACR) advocates for a fundamental shift in email security from static defense to protections that examine the entire business workflow. Email security must move from binary blocking to contextual understanding Because attackers have adapted to the controls organizations already deployed, SACR argues that email security must expand what it's expected to understand — from binary blocking to a contextual read on identity, relationships, workflow, intent, and behavior. That context matters because many modern attacks are designed to look ordinary at the message level. A vendor invoice, password reset, shared document, or executive request may not contain an obvious malicious attachment or known-bad link. The risk comes from how the message fits into a broader pattern: who appears to be involved, what action is being requested, whether the workflow makes sense, and how the interaction could expose credentials, data, or business processes if the user engages. Many of the most damaging attacks today look different. They exploit established relationships, legitimate infrastructure, identity workflows, and human decision-making under pressure. As a result, the current attack surface is not simply bad email; it is business workflow abused through email. Anna Perrone , Research Associate/Business Process Analyst at Software Analyst Cyber Research (SACR) Varonis Interceptor: from detection to investigation The SACR report highlights Varonis Interceptor as a leading example of the shift it sees reshaping the email security market. According to the report, Varonis approaches phishing not as a standalone messaging problem, but as the first stage of a broader attack chain that often culminates in credential theft, data exposure, privilege escalation, or business-process compromise. That framing, SACR argues, requires more than determining whether a single message is malicious — it requires understanding how attacks work, not simply whether they exist. The report describes Interceptor's architecture as built around that premise. Rather than relying on one detection method, the platform analyzes inbound communications using multiple detection layers — language models, visual analysis, infrastructure inspection, URL detonation, and behavioral indicators — to build a fuller picture of an attack before reaching a verdict. Varonis represents one of the clearest examples of a broader shift occurring within email security: the movement from detection toward investigation. Anna Perrone , Research Associate/Business Process Analyst at Software Analyst Cyber Research (SACR) To illustrate why this matters, the report walks through a scenario: a QR-code phishing attack that starts in an email, directs the user toward a trusted cloud service, routes them through several redirects, and ultimately lands on a credential-harvesting page built to mimic a familiar business application. At each individual step, the infrastructure involved looks legitimate, which is why the report argues that understanding how the stages connect matters more than evaluating any one link or domain in isolation. Varonis Interceptor’s AI Phishing Sandbox tests every potential action a user could take, applying zero trust to detect sophisticated email-based attacks. Varonis Interceptor’s AI Phishing Sandbox tests every potential action a user could take, applying zero trust to detect sophisticated email-based attacks. This exact challenge is one that SACR says Interceptor addresses with its AI Phishing Sandbox. The report notes it's designed to interact with phishing pages the way a person would. Interceptor follows every redirect, working through credential-capture forms, and surfacing multi-step attack paths to determine what a user would actually encounter if they followed the attack through to the end. The report notes this extends beyond the inbox as well: Interceptor's browser-oriented capabilities let it observe what users encounter after clicking a link, rather than stopping at the message itself. This gives security teams visibility into the full user journey that message inspection alone would miss. Why SACR says this matters now Phishing is becoming an identity and data problem, not just an inbox problem. The report points to Interceptor's data-security lineage as a distinct advantage: Varonis' data-centric background gives it a natural path into the questions that matter once an account is compromised — what sensitive data that account could reach, and whether the incident created broader exposure. Attacks no longer stay in one place. SACR's broader thesis is that today's attacks rarely stop at the inbox — a phishing email can lead to credential theft, identity compromise, and data exposure in the same incident. The report positions Interceptor as built to help teams answer the questions that follow: how the attack was delivered, what infrastructure was involved, whether users interacted with it, and what other systems may have been touched. AI has changed what a "suspicious" email looks like. The report ties this to its broader argument that generative AI has changed the cost structure of phishing, producing messages that are more personalized, more grammatically clean, and harder to distinguish from legitimate business communication. SACR frames Interceptor's multimodal, behavior-based analysis as a direct response to the fact that static, template-based detection struggles once every message can look slightly different. The future of email security is proof-driven SACR's report concludes that the future of email security won't be defined by a single architecture, but by how effectively different approaches help organizations understand attacks, respond efficiently, and reduce risk across an increasingly complex communication environment. Central to that argument is a shift the report identifies across the market as a whole: explainability is becoming a procurement requirement. Organizations need to know why a platform reached a conclusion, what evidence backs it up, and how a response decision can be defended to executives, auditors, regulators, and cyber insurers. Varonis Interceptor is presented in the report as one vendor built around that emerging generation of email security. Varonis applies an approach SACR characterizes as treating phishing detection, investigation, evidence generation, and remediation as connected parts of a single workflow, rather than isolated detection events.

title: Prezi Reviews: What Users Are Saying + My Honest Take [2026]
summary: Prezi reviews highlight fast, visually engaging presentations, but flag limits with AI features and exports. Here's what I found after testing it in 2026.
body_text: July 29th, 2026 Prezi Reviews: What Users Are Saying + My Honest Take [2026] By Tyler Shibata · 15 min read X LinkedIn Prezi reviews show a tool built for zoomable, motion-based presentations that move well beyond static slides. Some praise its visual impact and AI features, while others point to a learning curve and export limits. I built a deck from scratch and tried the AI presentation generator, then compared notes against recent G2 reviews to see where my experience lined up with everyone else's. Here's what stood out, its pros and cons, and whether it's worth your time in 2026. Quick verdict Prezi brings zoomable, motion-based design to presentations, built for people who want their slides to feel like one connected story. Reviews show that users appreciate the visual impact and how engaged it keeps an audience , but many say it takes a few full decks before the zoom-based format starts to click. The AI features go further than I expected for pulling together a first draft, but the export limits are worth planning around. Prezi does let you download a PPTX file, but it flattens every zoom and motion effect into static slides, so a client or teammate opening it in PowerPoint won't see the version you built. What is Prezi? Prezi is a presentation tool that replaces static slides with a single zoomable canvas , letting you pan and zoom between topics without clicking through separate pages. It uses motion and spatial layout to show how ideas connect, which is different from the slide-by-slide format in PowerPoint or Google Slides. The platform includes an AI presentation generator that builds a first draft from a prompt or document, along with templates, a video overlay feature for calls, and a stock image and icon library. Prezi runs in the browser and offers a free plan with limited features, plus paid tiers that unlock more storage, premium templates, and advanced customization. Key Prezi features Prezi covers the core needs for anyone who wants a presentation that feels less like a slideshow and more like a guided tour through an idea. Here's what the platform offers: Zoomable canvas: Build your whole presentation on one connected canvas, then zoom and pan between sections as you present. This is the feature that makes Prezi feel different the second you open it. AI presentation generator: Type a prompt or upload a document (PowerPoint, PDF, or Word) and Prezi AI builds a full draft with a theme, layout, and content already in place. I gave it a rough outline and had something usable in under a minute. Video overlay: Record yourself presenting directly over your slides without a green screen, so your face stays visible next to your content during calls or async recordings. Template library: Choose from a wide library of prebuilt templates, each with its own animation style you can preview by hovering over it before you commit. You can build your research presentation or sales report easily. Smart branding: Pull your brand colors and fonts automatically from your website or uploaded files, so a deck keeps a consistent look with your other materials without you setting each color by hand. Collaboration tools: Edit a presentation with teammates at the same time, leave comments, and manage who can view or edit each file. AI image generation and stock library: Generate custom visuals in a chosen style (photo, sketch, illustration) or pull from a stock library with over 150 million images, so you're not stuck hunting for the right graphic on your own. Viewer analytics: See who opened a shared presentation, which sections they spent time on, and for how long, available on Premium and Business plans. Handy if you're using Prezi for sales decks and want to know what actually lands. App integrations: Connect Prezi to tools like Zoom and Microsoft Teams to bring a presentation directly into a live call setup. Offline and portable presentations: Export a portable version through the desktop app so you can present without an internet connection. What real Prezi users are saying I read through recent Prezi reviews on G2 and Capterra to see what users think about the tool. Overall, people seem to genuinely like the zoom-based design and how fast it helps put a deck together. But reviews also flag a steep learning curve, limited export options, and a few features that stay locked behind a paid plan. Nothing shocking, but worth knowing before you commit. Here's what users are saying: Pros Dynamic, zoomable canvas: Prezi's zoom-based layout can make a presentation feel like one connected story. One enterprise reviewer said the transitions helped an audience understand how each slide connects to the bigger picture. Video overlay for calls: Prezi Video lets you show your slides right next to you during a call or recording. Reviewers say this can help hold attention on webinars and virtual demos, where it's easy for an audience to tune out. AI-assisted content generation: The built-in AI can suggest angles you may not have thought of on your own. One product manager said it gave them an expanded view of their original target , which is a nice bonus when you're staring at a blank canvas. Works from any computer: One founder said they can pull up their entire Prezi library from any computer, even without Wi-Fi, which makes it easier to present on the fly if your usual setup falls through. Faster, polished-looking decks: Several reviewers say Prezi cuts down time spent on formatting, which tracks with what I'd expect from a template-driven tool. One physician who builds training sessions said it let them create visually appealing decks in a fraction of the usual time . Cons Learning curve: New users may need real time to get comfortable with a zoom-based design, especially coming from PowerPoint or Keynote. Stock images tied to paid plans: Some images need an upgrade or extra credits to unlock. One reviewer on the free plan said certain images become hard to access without paying more. AI prompts can miss specialized topics: The AI may not fully understand niche or technical subject matter on the first try, so some reviewers say they end up doing extra edits to get the content right. Limited export options: Prezi does let you download a PPTX file, but the export flattens every zoom and motion effect into static slides. One reviewer said the PDF export strips the zoom and animation that make the tool worth using in the first place. Occasional autosave issues: A few reviewers mention their designs didn't always save the way they expected, which can mean redoing recent work. Always a gut punch when it happens. My personal take on Prezi Prezi turns a plain topic into a presentation people stay engaged with. The zoomable canvas makes a presentation feel like it's moving somewhere , and it beats clicking through the same 12 slides everyone's seen a version of. The AI generator got me from a blank canvas to a workable draft faster than I expected, and the templates carry their own personality, a step up from the same PowerPoint themes everyone recognizes on sight. That said, I found the format takes longer to master than the marketing suggests . Building a product presentation that zooms and pans in a way that helps your story without making your audience seasick takes a few tries to get right. The export situation is its own separate headache. You can get a PPTX file out of Prezi, but it flattens all the motion that made the deck worth building, so anyone expecting a clean handoff to a colleague on PowerPoint is in for a surprise. Prezi works well if you're presenting live, in the room or on a call , where the zoom and motion can actually land with an audience. If you need a deck that travels well between tools and teams, where half your coworkers are opening it in PowerPoint and the other half in Google Slides, the format starts working against you. Is Prezi right for you? After testing Prezi, I found it fits certain presentation styles far better than others. It's worth checking your own situation against a few specifics before committing. Here's how to tell if it fits your situation: Who will love it Anyone pitching the same story to different audiences: Prezi's Smart Branding and template system make it easy to reuse a core deck while swapping visuals and framing for each new audience, without rebuilding the whole thing from scratch. Teams that want to know if a presentation is landing: Viewer analytics on the Premium and Business plans show who opened a shared deck and how long they spent on each section, which is useful if you're sending decks out and want a signal beyond silence. People who present over video calls: The video overlay feature keeps you visible next to your content during a call, which is a small detail that makes remote presentations feel less like a static screen share. Anyone who wants outside inspiration during the design process: The AI image generator and large stock library take the pressure off finding the right visual on your own. Who should avoid it Anyone working from a locked internal reporting format: If your organization requires decks in a specific PowerPoint template with strict formatting rules, Prezi's canvas approach doesn't fit that structure. Teams without dedicated time to design: The templates and AI generator help, but getting a deck to feel intentional and avoid clutter still takes some hands-on attention. A team that just needs to throw bullet points on a slide may find that extra step a poor use of time. Anyone who needs to edit a shared file across many collaborators offline: Prezi's real-time co-editing is online-only. The desktop app's offline mode covers one person working without internet, with changes syncing back later. 💡 Tip: Not sold on Prezi? Check out our guide on the top Prezi competitors . The best Prezi alternative: Julius Prezi reviews highlight a distinctive, motion-based presentation style, but users consistently point to a learning curve, an export process that flattens the format, and AI features that stay limited to the presentation step itself. That last point matters if your presentations start with a spreadsheet, since Prezi can help you build the deck, but it won't touch the data behind it. Julius is a data analysis tool with a built-in presentation maker. We built it for people who need to go from raw numbers to a finished deck without switching between three separate tools to get there. Here's what you can do with Julius: Start from a question: Connect your own data, let Julius search the web for public datasets, or pull institutional-grade financials for over 17,000 companies through the Financial Datasets partnership , then ask Julius to turn any of it into a finished analysis. Turn an analysis into a presentation: Once Julius builds out your charts and insights, you can take that work straight into the AI presentation maker and skip rebuilding the same numbers from scratch in a separate deck. Get sharper answers the more you use it: With each query, Julius gets better at finding the right data within connected sources, so answers tend to get faster and more precise the more you ask. Schedule reports on a routine: A Notebook can run on a schedule and deliver updates straight to email or Slack, so you don’t need to rebuild reports by hand every week. If you want a tool that handles the data and the deck in one place, Julius is worth trying. Start analyzing your data with Julius today . Final verdict If you need a presentation style built around movement and live audience engagement, Prezi delivers. But if the export limits, learning curve, or standalone AI tools are working against your workflow, Julius is worth considering . Frequently asked questions Is Prezi free to use? Yes, Prezi offers a free plan called Basic , which gives you limited AI credits and access to core tools. Paid plans start with Standard, and Plus is where you unlock offline access through the desktop app, presenter features, and personal branding, with Premium adding viewer analytics and phone support. Does Prezi still get updated in 2026? Yes, Prezi continues to release updates in 2026 , with recent additions including AI-generated charts, cinematic illustrated backdrops, and viewer analytics you can review directly through the AI. New designer themes and quiz generation from existing decks have also rolled out this year. The platform is actively maintained rather than left on a legacy feature set. Can you export Prezi to PowerPoint? Yes, you can export a Prezi presentation as a PPTX file directly from the Share menu in the editor. The export flattens each frame into a static PowerPoint slide, so the zoom and motion effects don't carry over. A PDF export is also available if you only need the presentation viewable, not editable.
